title: When Shopping Had a Soundtrack
titleZh: 买东西也有背景声的年代
paras: Before fixed-price shops became common, street sellers brought everyday shopping to the doorstep. In European cities, their cries announced bread, fish and other [[merchandise|merchandise]]. A seller might enter a shared [[courtyard|courtyard]], where one shout could reach several households. These calls saved customers a journey and helped sellers attract attention without paying for a permanent shop.

By the seventeenth century, printed pictures of street traders often included their familiar calls. The language was brief rather than complete: [[grammatical|grammatical]] rules mattered less than a clear rhythm and a recognisable product name. For [[instance|instance]], a fish seller could repeat the name of a fresh catch, stretching its vowels into a tune. Claims that goods were fresh or [[edible|edible]], however, were not guarantees of quality.

Selling by voice required skill. Carts could [[collide|collide]] in narrow streets, while wind might [[howl|howl]] between buildings and drown out a carefully practised call. Heavy rain could [[disrupt|disrupt]] trade altogether. Sellers also needed to judge their audience: a cry loud enough for an open square was not necessarily [[satisfactory|satisfactory]] beneath a bedroom window.

During the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, expanding shop networks and restrictions on street noise changed this soundscape. As familiar calls became less common, musicians and collectors began treating them as a [[threatened|threatened]] part of urban culture. Written music and, later, sound recordings preserved some examples. What had once been an ordinary invitation to buy became evidence of how a city had listened.
zh: 在明码标价的商店普及之前，街头小贩把日常购物带到了人们家门口。在欧洲城市，他们通过叫卖声推销面包、鱼和其他商品。小贩可能走进一个共用的庭院，在那里，一声吆喝就能让好几户人家听见。这些叫卖声让顾客少跑一趟，也让小贩不必花钱租用固定店面就能吸引注意。
到了十七世纪，描绘街头商贩的印刷图画常常会配上人们熟悉的叫卖词。这些话简短而非完整：比起语法规则，清晰的节奏和容易辨认的商品名称更重要。例如，鱼贩可以反复喊出刚捕到的鱼的名字，把元音拖长，形成曲调。然而，声称商品新鲜或可以食用，并不等于保证了质量。
靠声音做买卖需要技巧。手推车可能在狭窄的街道上相撞，风也可能在楼房之间呼啸，淹没精心练习过的叫卖声。大雨甚至会让生意完全中断。小贩还需要判断听众的情况：在开阔广场上足够响亮的叫卖声，到了卧室窗下就未必合适了。
十九至二十世纪，不断扩大的商店网络和对街头噪声的限制改变了这片城市声景。随着熟悉的叫卖声越来越少，音乐家和收集者开始将其视为城市文化中面临消失威胁的一部分。乐谱以及后来出现的录音保存了其中一些声音。曾经寻常的购物邀请，就这样成了了解一座城市昔日听觉生活的证据。

q.s: Calling out in a shared residential space allowed a trader to advertise to several homes at once.
q.why: 首段指出，庭院里一声吆喝可传到几户人家。

q.s: Street sellers valued correct sentence structure more than the rhythm of their calls.
q.why: 第二段指出，语法不如清晰的节奏重要。

q.s: Collectors paid street sellers to make sound recordings of their calls.
q.why: 末段提到录音保存叫卖声，未提及付费。
